<h3 id="listalleventforuser-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Used to view events. Events are automatically created and contain information about everything that happens to your bunq account. In the bunq app events are shown in your 'overview'. Examples of when events are created or modified: payment sent, payment received, request for payment received or connect invite received.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

<h3 id="listalleventforuser-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[EventListing](#schemaeventlisting)]|false|none|none|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|200|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|400|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## READ_Event_for_User

<a id="opIdREAD_Event_for_User"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/event/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /user/{userID}/event/{itemId}`

Get a specific event for a given user.

<h3 id="readeventforuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|itemId|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

<h1 id="bunq-api-export-annual-overview">export-annual-overview</h1>

## List_all_ExportAnnualOverview_for_User

<a id="opIdList_all_ExportAnnualOverview_for_User"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/export-annual-overview \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /user/{userID}/export-annual-overview`

List all the annual overviews for a user.

<h3 id="listallexportannualoverviewforuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

<h1 id="bunq-api-insights-search">insights-search</h1>

## List_all_InsightsSearch_for_User

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/insights-search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /user/{userID}/insights-search`

Used to get events based on time and insight category.

<h3 id="listallinsightssearchforuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

## List_all_Installation

<a id="opIdList_all_Installation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/installation \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /installation`

You must have an active session to make this call. This call returns the Id of the the Installation you are using in your session.

<h3 id="listallinstallation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": 0
  }
]
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "Error": [
    {
      "error_description": "string",
      "error_description_translated": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

Additionally, you can use the token you get from an Installation to authenticate the registration of a new device.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

## CREATE_Installation

<a id="opIdCREATE_Installation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/installation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string' \
  -d '{
    "client_public_key": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /installation`

This is the only API call that does not require you to use the "X-Bunq-Client-Authentication" and "X-Bunq-Client-Signature" headers.
 You provide the server with the public part of the key pair that you are going to use to create the value of the signature header for all future API calls. The server creates an installation for you. Store the Installation Token and ServerPublicKey from the response. This token is used in the "X-Bunq-Client-Authentication" header for the creation of a DeviceServer and SessionServer.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_public_key": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createinstallation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|
|body|body|[Installation](#schemainstallation)|true|none|
|» client_public_key|body|string|true|Your public key. This is the public part of the key pair that you are going to use to create value of the "X-Bunq-Client-Signature" header for all future API calls.|

`GET /user/{userID}/monetary-account`

Get a collection of all your MonetaryAccounts.

<h3 id="listallmonetaryaccountforuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

```bash
  -d '{
    "avatar_uuid": "string",

    "currency": "string",
    "daily_limit": {
      "currency": "string",
      "value": "string"
    },
    "description": "string",
    "display_name": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "reason_description": "string",
    "setting": {
      "color": "string",
      "default_avatar_status": "string",
      "icon": "string",
      "restriction_chat": "string",
      "sdd_expiration_action": "string"
    },
    "status": "string",
    "sub_status": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /user/{userID}/monetary-account-bank`

Create new MonetaryAccountBank.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "avatar_uuid": "string",
  "country_iban": "string",
  "currency": "string",
  "daily_limit": {
    "currency": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "description": "string",
  "display_name": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "reason_description": "string",
  "setting": {
    "color": "string",
    "default_avatar_status": "string",
    "icon": "string",
    "restriction_chat": "string",
    "sdd_expiration_action": "string"
  },
  "status": "string",
  "sub_status": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createmonetaryaccountbankforuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|
|body|body|[MonetaryAccountBank](#schemamonetaryaccountbank)|true|none|
|» avatar_uuid|body|string|false|The UUID of the Avatar of the MonetaryAccountBank.|
|» country_iban|body|string|false|The country of the monetary account IBAN.|
|» currency|body|string|true|The currency of the MonetaryAccountBank as an ISO 4217 formatted currency code.|
|» daily_limit|body|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|The daily spending limit Amount of the MonetaryAccountBank. Defaults to 1000 EUR. Currency must match the MonetaryAccountBank's currency. Limited to 10000 EUR.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the MonetaryAccountBank. Defaults to 'bunq account'.|
|» display_name|body|string|false|The legal name of the user / company using this monetary account.|
|» reason|body|string|false|The reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountBank, can only be OTHER. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» reason_description|body|string|false|The optional free-form reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountBank. Can be any user provided message. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» setting|body|[MonetaryAccountSetting](#schemamonetaryaccountsetting)|false|The settings of the MonetaryAccountBank.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the MonetaryAccountBank. Ignored in POST requests (always set to ACTIVE) can be CANCELLED or PENDING_REOPEN in PUT requests to cancel (close) or reopen the MonetaryAccountBank. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|
|» sub_status|body|string|false|The sub-status of the MonetaryAccountBank providing extra information regarding the status. Should be ignored for POST requests. In case of PUT requests with status CANCELLED it can only be REDEMPTION_VOLUNTARY, while with status PENDING_REOPEN it can only be NONE. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

|» avatar_uuid|body|string|false|The UUID of the Avatar of the MonetaryAccountBank.|

|» description|body|string|false|The description of the MonetaryAccountBank. Defaults to 'bunq account'.|
|» display_name|body|string|false|The legal name of the user / company using this monetary account.|
|» reason|body|string|false|The reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountBank, can only be OTHER. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» reason_description|body|string|false|The optional free-form reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountBank. Can be any user provided message. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|

When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|
|» sub_status|body|string|false|The sub-status of the MonetaryAccountBank providing extra information regarding the status. Should be ignored for POST requests. In case of PUT requests with status CANCELLED it can only be REDEMPTION_VOLUNTARY, while with status PENDING_REOPEN it can only be NONE. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|

|» alias|body|[[Pointer](#schemapointer)]|false|The Aliases to add to MonetaryAccountJoint. Must all be confirmed first. Can mostly be ignored.|

|» description|body|string|false|The description of the MonetaryAccountJoint. Defaults to 'bunq account'.|
|» overdraft_limit|body|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|The maximum Amount the MonetaryAccountJoint can be 'in the red'. Must be 0 EUR or omitted.|
|» reason|body|string|false|The reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountJoint, can only be OTHER. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» reason_description|body|string|false|The optional free-form reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountJoint. Can be any user provided message. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» setting|body|[MonetaryAccountSetting](#schemamonetaryaccountsetting)|false|The settings of the MonetaryAccountJoint.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the MonetaryAccountJoint. Ignored in POST requests (always set to ACTIVE) can be CANCELLED or PENDING_REOPEN in PUT requests to cancel (close) or reopen the MonetaryAccountJoint. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|
|» sub_status|body|string|false|The sub-status of the MonetaryAccountJoint providing extra information regarding the status. Should be ignored for POST requests. In case of PUT requests with status CANCELLED it can only be REDEMPTION_VOLUNTARY, while with status PENDING_REOPEN it can only be NONE. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|

|body|body|[MonetaryAccountJoint](#schemamonetaryaccountjoint)|true|none|
|» alias|body|[[Pointer](#schemapointer)]|false|The Aliases to add to MonetaryAccountJoint. Must all be confirmed first. Can mostly be ignored.|
|» all_co_owner|body|[[CoOwner](#schemacoowner)]|true|The users the account will be joint with.|
|» avatar_uuid|body|string|false|The UUID of the Avatar of the MonetaryAccountJoint.|
|» currency|body|string|true|The currency of the MonetaryAccountJoint as an ISO 4217 formatted currency code.|
|» daily_limit|body|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|The daily spending limit Amount of the MonetaryAccountJoint. Defaults to 1000 EUR. Currency must match the MonetaryAccountJoint's currency. Limited to 10000 EUR.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the MonetaryAccountJoint. Defaults to 'bunq account'.|
|» overdraft_limit|body|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|The maximum Amount the MonetaryAccountJoint can be 'in the red'. Must be 0 EUR or omitted.|
|» reason|body|string|false|The reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountJoint, can only be OTHER. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» reason_description|body|string|false|The optional free-form reason for voluntarily cancelling (closing) the MonetaryAccountJoint. Can be any user provided message. Should only be specified if updating the status to CANCELLED.|
|» setting|body|[MonetaryAccountSetting](#schemamonetaryaccountsetting)|false|The settings of the MonetaryAccountJoint.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the MonetaryAccountJoint. Ignored in POST requests (always set to ACTIVE) can be CANCELLED or PENDING_REOPEN in PUT requests to cancel (close) or reopen the MonetaryAccountJoint. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|
|» sub_status|body|string|false|The sub-status of the MonetaryAccountJoint providing extra information regarding the status. Should be ignored for POST requests. In case of PUT requests with status CANCELLED it can only be REDEMPTION_VOLUNTARY, while with status PENDING_REOPEN it can only be NONE. When updating the status and/or sub_status no other fields can be updated in the same request (and vice versa).|

<h1 id="bunq-api-replace">replace</h1>

## CREATE_Replace_for_User_Card

<a id="opIdCREATE_Replace_for_User_Card"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/card/0/replace \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string' \
  -d '{
    "name_on_card": "string",
    "pin_code_assignment": [
      {
        "monetary_account_id": 0,
        "pin_code": "string",
        "routing_type": "string",
        "type": "string"
      }
    ],
    "preferred_name_on_card": "string",
    "second_line": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /user/{userID}/card/{cardID}/replace`

Request a card replacement.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name_on_card": "string",
  "pin_code_assignment": [
    {
      "monetary_account_id": 0,
      "pin_code": "string",
      "routing_type": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "preferred_name_on_card": "string",
  "second_line": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createreplaceforusercard-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|cardID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|
|body|body|[CardReplace](#schemacardreplace)|true|none|
|» name_on_card|body|string|false|The user's name as it will be on the card. Check 'card-name' for the available card names for a user.|
|» pin_code_assignment|body|[[CardPinAssignment](#schemacardpinassignment)]|false|Array of Types, PINs, account IDs assigned to the card.|
|» preferred_name_on_card|body|string|false|The user's preferred name that can be put on the card.|
|» second_line|body|string|false|The second line on the card.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "Id": {
    "id": 0
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "Error": [
    {
      "error_description": "string",
      "error_description_translated": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|It is possible to order a card replacement with the bunq API.<br/><br/>You can order up to one free card replacement per year. Additional replacement requests will be billed.<br/><br/>The card replacement will have the same expiry date and the same pricing as the old card, but it will have a new card number. You can change the description and optional the PIN through the card replacement endpoint.|[CardReplaceCreate](#schemacardreplacecreate)|
|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

`POST /user/{userID}/monetary-account/{monetary-accountID}/request-inquiry`

Create a new payment request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_amount_higher": true,
  "allow_amount_lower": true,
  "allow_bunqme": true,
  "amount_inquired": {
    "currency": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "attachment": [
    {
      "id": 0
    }
  ],
  "counterparty_alias": {},
  "description": "string",
  "event_id": 0,
  "merchant_reference": "string",
  "minimum_age": 0,
  "redirect_url": "string",
  "require_address": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "want_tip": true
}
```

<h3 id="createrequestinquiryforusermonetaryaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|monetary-accountID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|
|body|body|[RequestInquiry](#schemarequestinquiry)|true|none|
|» allow_amount_higher|body|boolean|false|[DEPRECATED] Whether or not the accepting user can choose to accept with a higher amount than requested. Defaults to false.|
|» allow_amount_lower|body|boolean|false|[DEPRECATED] Whether or not the accepting user can choose to accept with a lower amount than requested. Defaults to false.|
|» allow_bunqme|body|boolean|true|Whether or not sending a bunq.me request is allowed.|
|» amount_inquired|body|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|The requested amount.|
|» attachment|body|[[BunqId](#schemabunqid)]|false|The attachments attached to the payment.|
|» counterparty_alias|body|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|The LabelMonetaryAccount with the public information of the MonetaryAccount the money was requested from.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the inquiry.|
|» event_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the associated event if the request was made using 'split the bill'.|
|» merchant_reference|body|string|false|The client's custom reference that was attached to the request and the mutation.|
|» minimum_age|body|integer|false|The minimum age the user accepting the RequestInquiry must have.|
|» redirect_url|body|string|false|The URL which the user is sent to after accepting or rejecting the Request.|
|» require_address|body|string|false|Whether or not an address must be provided on accept.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the request.|
|» want_tip|body|boolean|false|[DEPRECATED] Whether or not the accepting user can give an extra tip on top of the requested Amount. Defaults to false.|

<h3 id="readrequestinquiryforusermonetaryaccount-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|RequestInquiry, aka 'RFP' (Request for Payment), is one of the innovative features that bunq offers. To request payment from another bunq account a new Request Inquiry is created. As with payments you can add attachments to a RFP. Requests for Payment are the foundation for a number of consumer features like 'Split the bill' and 'Request forwarding'. We invite you to invent your own based on the bunq api!|[RequestInquiryRead](#schemarequestinquiryread)|
|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

<h3 id="readrequestinquiryforusermonetaryaccount-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|200|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|

`PUT /user/{userID}/monetary-account/{monetary-accountID}/request-inquiry/{itemId}`

Revoke a request for payment, by updating the status to REVOKED.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "allow_amount_higher": true,
  "allow_amount_lower": true,
  "allow_bunqme": true,
  "amount_inquired": {
    "currency": "string",
    "value": "string"
  },
  "attachment": [
    {
      "id": 0
    }
  ],
  "counterparty_alias": {},
  "description": "string",
  "event_id": 0,
  "merchant_reference": "string",
  "minimum_age": 0,
  "redirect_url": "string",
  "require_address": "string",
  "status": "string",
  "want_tip": true
}
```

<h3 id="updaterequestinquiryforusermonetaryaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|monetary-accountID|path|integer|true|none|
|itemId|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|
|body|body|[RequestInquiry](#schemarequestinquiry)|true|none|
|» allow_amount_higher|body|boolean|false|[DEPRECATED] Whether or not the accepting user can choose to accept with a higher amount than requested. Defaults to false.|
|» allow_amount_lower|body|boolean|false|[DEPRECATED] Whether or not the accepting user can choose to accept with a lower amount than requested. Defaults to false.|
|» allow_bunqme|body|boolean|true|Whether or not sending a bunq.me request is allowed.|
|» amount_inquired|body|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|The requested amount.|
|» attachment|body|[[BunqId](#schemabunqid)]|false|The attachments attached to the payment.|
|» counterparty_alias|body|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|The LabelMonetaryAccount with the public information of the MonetaryAccount the money was requested from.|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the inquiry.|
|» event_id|body|integer|false|The ID of the associated event if the request was made using 'split the bill'.|
|» merchant_reference|body|string|false|The client's custom reference that was attached to the request and the mutation.|
|» minimum_age|body|integer|false|The minimum age the user accepting the RequestInquiry must have.|
|» redirect_url|body|string|false|The URL which the user is sent to after accepting or rejecting the Request.|
|» require_address|body|string|false|Whether or not an address must be provided on accept.|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the request.|
|» want_tip|body|boolean|false|[DEPRECATED] Whether or not the accepting user can give an extra tip on top of the requested Amount. Defaults to false.|

<h3 id="updaterequestinquiryforusermonetaryaccount-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|RequestInquiry, aka 'RFP' (Request for Payment), is one of the innovative features that bunq offers. To request payment from another bunq account a new Request Inquiry is created. As with payments you can add attachments to a RFP. Requests for Payment are the foundation for a number of consumer features like 'Split the bill' and 'Request forwarding'. We invite you to invent your own based on the bunq api!|[RequestInquiryUpdate](#schemarequestinquiryupdate)|
|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

<h1 id="bunq-api-request-inquiry-batch">request-inquiry-batch</h1>

## List_all_RequestInquiryBatch_for_User_MonetaryAccount

<a id="opIdList_all_RequestInquiryBatch_for_User_MonetaryAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/monetary-account/0/request-inquiry-batch \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /user/{userID}/monetary-account/{monetary-accountID}/request-inquiry-batch`

Return all the request batches for a monetary account.

<h3 id="listallrequestinquirybatchforusermonetaryaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|userID|path|integer|true|none|
|monetary-accountID|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A RequestResponse is what a user on the other side of a RequestInquiry gets when he is sent one. So a RequestInquiry is the initiator and visible for the user that sent it and that wants to receive the money. `POST /session-server`

Create a new session for a DeviceServer. Provide the Installation token in the "X-Bunq-Client-Authentication" header. And don't forget to create the "X-Bunq-Client-Signature" header. The response contains a Session token that should be used for as the "X-Bunq-Client-Authentication" header for all future API calls. The ip address making this call needs to match the ip address bound to your API key.

```json
}
```

<h3 id="createsessionserver-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Once you have created an Installation and a DeviceServer with that Installation, then you are ready to start a session! A session expires after the same amount of time you have set for Auto Logout in your user account. By default this is 1 week. If a request is made 30 seconds before a session expires, it will be extended from that moment by your auto logout time, but never by more than 5 minutes.|[SessionServerCreate](#schemasessionservercreate)|
|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

<h3 id="createsessionserver-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|200|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|400|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|

<h1 id="bunq-api-share-invite-monetary-account-inquiry">share-invite-monetary-account-inquiry</h1>

## List_all_ShareInviteMonetaryAccountInquiry_for_User_MonetaryAccount

<a id="opIdList_all_ShareInviteMonetaryAccountInquiry_for_User_MonetaryAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/monetary-account/0/share-invite-monetary-account-inquiry \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /user/{userID}/monetary-account/{monetary-accountID}/share-invite-monetary-account-inquiry`

[DEPRECATED - use /share-invite-monetary-account-response] Get a list with all the share inquiries for a monetary account, only if the requesting user has permission to change the details of the various ones.

<h3 id="listallshareinvitemonetaryaccountinquiryforusermonetaryaccount-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h3 id="listalluser-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|This is how the error response looks like for 4XX response codes|Inline|

<h3 id="listalluser-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[UserListing](#schemauserlisting)]|false|none|none|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|false|none|none|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|200|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|200|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|string||This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|400|X-Bunq-Client-Response-Id|string||A unique ID for the response formatted as a UUID. Clients can use it to add extra protection against replay attacks.|
|400|X-Bunq-Server-Signature|string||The server's signature for this response. See the signing page for details on how to verify this signature.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## READ_User

<a id="opIdREAD_User"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`GET /user/{itemId}`

Get a specific user.

<h3 id="readuser-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|itemId|path|integer|true|none|
|Cache-Control|header|string|false|The standard HTTP Cache-Control header is required for all signed requests.|
|User-Agent|header|string|true|The User-Agent header field should contain information about the user agent originating the request. There are no restrictions on the value of this header.|
|X-Bunq-Language|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Language header must contain a preferred language indication. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore. Currently only the languages en_US and nl_NL are supported. Anything else will default to en_US.|
|X-Bunq-Region|header|string|false|The X-Bunq-Region header must contain the region (country) of the client device. The value of this header is formatted as a ISO 639-1 language code plus a ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, separated by an underscore.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Request-Id|header|string|false|This header must specify an ID with each request that is unique for the logged in user. There are no restrictions for the format of this ID. However, the server will respond with an error when the same ID is used again on the same DeviceServer.|
|X-Bunq-Geolocation|header|string|false|This header must specify the geolocation of the device. The format of this value is longitude latitude altitude radius country. The country is expected to be formatted of an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. When no geolocation is available or known the header must still be included but can be zero valued.|
|X-Bunq-Client-Authentication|header|string|true|The authentication token is used to authenticate the source of the API call. It is required by all API calls except for POST /v1/installation. It is important to note that the device and session calls are using the token from the response of the installation call, while all the other calls use the token from the response of the session-server call|

## DELETE_WhitelistSddRecurring_for_User

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/user/0/whitelist-sdd-recurring/0 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'User-Agent: string' \
  -H 'X-Bunq-Client-Authentication: string'
```

`DELETE /user/{userID}/whitelist-sdd-recurring/{itemId}`

Whitelist a recurring SDD so that when another recurrence comes in, it is automatically accepted.

|subscription_type_downgrade|string|false|read-only|The subscription type the user will have after a subscription downgrade. Will be null if downgrading is not possible.|
|updated|string|false|read-only|The timestamp when the billing contract was last updated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|bunqme_tab_entry|[BunqMeTabEntry](#schemabunqmetabentry)|false|none|The bunq.me entry containing the payment information.|
|bunqme_tab_share_url|string|false|read-only|The url that points to the bunq.me page.|
|created|string|false|read-only|The timestamp when the bunq.me was created.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the created bunq.me.|
|monetary_account_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the MonetaryAccount the bunq.me was sent from.|
|result_inquiries|[[BunqMeTabResultInquiry](#schemabunqmetabresultinquiry)]|false|read-only|The list of bunq.me result Inquiries successfully made and paid.|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status of the bunq.me. Can be WAITING_FOR_PAYMENT, CANCELLED or EXPIRED.|
|time_expiry|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of when the bunq.me expired or will expire.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the bunq.me Tab. Should be BUNQ_ME|
|updated|string|false|read-only|The timestamp when the bunq.me was last updated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|activation_code|string|false|write-only|DEPRECATED: Activate a card by setting status to ACTIVE when the order_status is ACCEPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION.|
|card_limit|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The spending limit for the card.|
|card_limit_atm|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The ATM spending limit for the card.|
|country_permission|[[CardCountryPermission](#schemacardcountrypermission)]|false|none|The countries for which to grant (temporary) permissions to use the card.|
|monetary_account_id_fallback|integer|false|none|ID of the MA to be used as fallback for this card if insufficient balance. Fallback account is removed if not supplied.|
|order_status|string|false|none|The order status to set for the card. Set to CARD_REQUEST_PENDING to get a virtual card produced.|
|pin_code|string|false|write-only|The plaintext pin code. Requests require encryption to be enabled.|
|pin_code_assignment|[[CardPinAssignment](#schemacardpinassignment)]|false|none|Array of Types, PINs, account IDs assigned to the card.|
|primary_account_numbers|[[CardPrimaryAccountNumber](#schemacardprimaryaccountnumber)]|false|none|Array of PANs and their attributes.|
|status|string|false|none|The status to set for the card. Can be ACTIVE, DEACTIVATED, LOST, STOLEN or CANCELLED, and can only be set to LOST/STOLEN/CANCELLED when order status is ACCEPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION/DELIVERED_TO_CUSTOMER/CARD_UPDATE_REQUESTED/CARD_UPDATE_SENT/CARD_UPDATE_ACCEPTED. Can only be set to DEACTIVATED after initial activation, i.e. order_status is DELIVERED_TO_CUSTOMER/CARD_UPDATE_REQUESTED/CARD_UPDATE_SENT/CARD_UPDATE_ACCEPTED. Mind that all the possible choices (apart from ACTIVE and DEACTIVATED) are permanent and cannot be changed after.|

|card_limit|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The spending limit for the card.|
|card_limit_atm|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The ATM spending limit for the card.|
|country_permission|[[CardCountryPermission](#schemacardcountrypermission)]|false|write-only|The countries for which to grant (temporary) permissions to use the card.|
|id|integer|true|write-only|The ID of the card that needs to be updated.|
|monetary_account_id_fallback|integer|false|write-only|ID of the MA to be used as fallback for this card if insufficient balance. Fallback account is removed if not supplied.|
|status|string|false|write-only|The status to set for the card. Can be ACTIVE, DEACTIVATED, LOST, STOLEN or CANCELLED, and can only be set to LOST/STOLEN/CANCELLED when order status is ACCEPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION/DELIVERED_TO_CUSTOMER/CARD_UPDATE_REQUESTED/CARD_UPDATE_SENT/CARD_UPDATE_ACCEPTED. Can only be set to DEACTIVATED after initial activation, i.e. order_status is DELIVERED_TO_CUSTOMER/CARD_UPDATE_REQUESTED/CARD_UPDATE_SENT/CARD_UPDATE_ACCEPTED. Mind that all the possible choices (apart from ACTIVE and DEACTIVATED) are permanent and cannot be changed after.|

|---|---|---|---|---|

|product_type|string|true|none|The product type of the card to order.|
|second_line|string|true|none|The second line of text on the card, used as name/description for it. It can contain at most 17 characters and it can be empty.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of card to order. Can be MASTERCARD.|

|monetary_account_id_fallback|integer|false|read-only|ID of the MA to be used as fallback for this card if insufficient balance. Fallback account is removed if not supplied.|
|name_on_card|string|false|read-only|The user's name on the card.|
|order_status|string|false|read-only|The order status of the card. Can be NEW_CARD_REQUEST_RECEIVED, CARD_REQUEST_PENDING, SENT_FOR_PRODUCTION, ACCEPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION, DELIVERED_TO_CUSTOMER, CARD_UPDATE_REQUESTED, CARD_UPDATE_PENDING, CARD_UPDATE_SENT, CARD_UPDATE_ACCEPTED, VIRTUAL_DELIVERY, NEW_CARD_REQUEST_PENDING_USER_APPROVAL, SENT_FOR_DELIVERY or NEW_CARD_REQUEST_CANCELLED.|
|payment_account_reference|string|false|read-only|The payment account reference number associated with the card.|
|pin_code_assignment|[[CardPinAssignment](#schemacardpinassignment)]|false|read-only|Array of Types, PINs, account IDs assigned to the card.|
|primary_account_numbers|[[CardPrimaryAccountNumber](#schemacardprimaryaccountnumber)]|false|read-only|Array of PANs and their attributes.|
|public_uuid|string|false|read-only|The public UUID of the card.|
|second_line|string|false|read-only|The second line of text on the card|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status to set for the card. Can be ACTIVE, DEACTIVATED, LOST, STOLEN, CANCELLED, EXPIRED or PIN_TRIES_EXCEEDED.|
|sub_status|string|false|read-only|The sub-status of the card. Can be NONE or REPLACED.|
|sub_type|string|false|read-only|The sub-type of the card.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the card. Can be MAESTRO, MASTERCARD.|
|updated|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the card's last update.|
|user_id|integer|false|read-only|ID of the user who is owner of the card.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|card_limit|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The spending limit for the card.|
|card_limit_atm|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The ATM spending limit for the card.|
|card_shipment_tracking_url|string|false|read-only|A tracking link provided by our shipment provider.|
|country|string|false|read-only|The country that is domestic to the card. Defaults to country of residence of user.|
|country_permission|[[CardCountryPermission](#schemacardcountrypermission)]|false|read-only|The countries for which to grant (temporary) permissions to use the card.|
|created|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the card's creation.|
|expiry_date|string|false|read-only|Expiry date of the card.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the card.|
|label_monetary_account_current|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The monetary account that this card is currently linked to and the label user viewing it.|
|label_monetary_account_ordered|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The monetary account this card was ordered on and the label user that owns the card.|
|monetary_account_id_fallback|integer|false|read-only|ID of the MA to be used as fallback for this card if insufficient balance. Fallback account is removed if not supplied.|
|name_on_card|string|false|read-only|The user's name on the card.|
|order_status|string|false|read-only|The order status of the card. Can be NEW_CARD_REQUEST_RECEIVED, CARD_REQUEST_PENDING, SENT_FOR_PRODUCTION, ACCEPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION, DELIVERED_TO_CUSTOMER, CARD_UPDATE_REQUESTED, CARD_UPDATE_PENDING, CARD_UPDATE_SENT, CARD_UPDATE_ACCEPTED, VIRTUAL_DELIVERY, NEW_CARD_REQUEST_PENDING_USER_APPROVAL, SENT_FOR_DELIVERY or NEW_CARD_REQUEST_CANCELLED.|
|payment_account_reference|string|false|read-only|The payment account reference number associated with the card.|
|pin_code_assignment|[[CardPinAssignment](#schemacardpinassignment)]|false|read-only|Array of Types, PINs, account IDs assigned to the card.|
|primary_account_numbers|[[CardPrimaryAccountNumber](#schemacardprimaryaccountnumber)]|false|read-only|Array of PANs and their attributes.|
|public_uuid|string|false|read-only|The public UUID of the card.|
|second_line|string|false|read-only|The second line of text on the card|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status to set for the card. Can be ACTIVE, DEACTIVATED, LOST, STOLEN, CANCELLED, EXPIRED or PIN_TRIES_EXCEEDED.|
|sub_status|string|false|read-only|The sub-status of the card. Can be NONE or REPLACED.|
|sub_type|string|false|read-only|The sub-type of the card.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the card. Can be MAESTRO, MASTERCARD.|
|updated|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the card's last update.|
|user_id|integer|false|read-only|ID of the user who is owner of the card.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alias|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The LabelMonetaryAccount containing the public information of 'this' (party) side of the DraftPayment.|
|amount|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the payment.|
|attachment|[[AttachmentMonetaryAccountPayment](#schemaattachmentmonetaryaccountpayment)]|false|none|The Attachments attached to the DraftPayment.|
|counterparty_alias|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The LabelMonetaryAccount containing the public information of the other (counterparty) side of the DraftPayment.|
|description|string|false|none|The description for the DraftPayment. Maximum 140 characters for DraftPayments to external IBANs, 9000 characters for DraftPayments to only other bunq MonetaryAccounts.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the draft payment entry.|
|merchant_reference|string|false|none|Optional data to be included with the Payment specific to the merchant.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the draft payment entry.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the created DrafPayment.|
|monetary_account_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the MonetaryAccount the DraftPayment applies to.|
|object|[DraftPaymentAnchorObject](#schemadraftpaymentanchorobject)|false|none|The Payment or PaymentBatch. This will only be present after the DraftPayment has been accepted.|
|request_reference_split_the_bill|[[RequestInquiryReference](#schemarequestinquiryreference)]|false|read-only|The reference to the object used for split the bill. Can be RequestInquiry or RequestInquiryBatch|
|responses|[[DraftPaymentResponse](#schemadraftpaymentresponse)]|false|read-only|All responses to this draft payment.|
|schedule|[Schedule](#schemaschedule)|false|none|The schedule details.|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status of the DraftPayment.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the DraftPayment.|
|user_alias_created|[LabelUser](#schemalabeluser)|false|none|The label of the User who created the DraftPayment.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|entries|[[DraftPaymentEntry](#schemadraftpaymententry)]|false|read-only|The entries in the DraftPayment.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the created DrafPayment.|
|monetary_account_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the MonetaryAccount the DraftPayment applies to.|
|object|[DraftPaymentAnchorObject](#schemadraftpaymentanchorobject)|false|none|The Payment or PaymentBatch. This will only be present after the DraftPayment has been accepted.|
|request_reference_split_the_bill|[[RequestInquiryReference](#schemarequestinquiryreference)]|false|read-only|The reference to the object used for split the bill. Can be RequestInquiry or RequestInquiryBatch|
|responses|[[DraftPaymentResponse](#schemadraftpaymentresponse)]|false|read-only|All responses to this draft payment.|
|schedule|[Schedule](#schemaschedule)|false|none|The schedule details.|
|status|string|false|read-only|The status of the DraftPayment.|
|type|string|false|read-only|The type of the DraftPayment.|
|user_alias_created|[LabelUser](#schemalabeluser)|false|none|The label of the User who created the DraftPayment.|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|false|read-only|The performed action. Can be: CREATE or UPDATE.|
|created|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the event's creation.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the event.|
|monetary_account_id|string|false|read-only|The id of the monetary account the event applied to (if it was a monetary account event).|
|object|[EventObject](#schemaeventobject)|false|none|The details of the external object the event was created for.|
|status|string|false|read-only|The event status. Can be: FINALIZED or AWAITING_REPLY. An example of FINALIZED event is a payment received event, while an AWAITING_REPLY event is a request received event.|
|updated|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the event's last update.|
|user_id|string|false|read-only|The id of the user the event applied to (if it was a user event).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action|string|false|read-only|The performed action. Can be: CREATE or UPDATE.|
|created|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the event's creation.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the event.|
|monetary_account_id|string|false|read-only|The id of the monetary account the event applied to (if it was a monetary account event).|
|object|[EventObject](#schemaeventobject)|false|none|The details of the external object the event was created for.|
|status|string|false|read-only|The event status. Can be: FINALIZED or AWAITING_REPLY. An example of FINALIZED event is a payment received event, while an AWAITING_REPLY event is a request received event.|
|updated|string|false|read-only|The timestamp of the event's last update.|
|user_id|string|false|read-only|The id of the user the event applied to (if it was a user event).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date_end|string|true|none|The end date for making statements.|
|date_start|string|true|none|The start date for making statements.|

|statement_format|string|true|none|The format type of statement. Allowed values: MT940, CSV, PDF.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alias|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The monetary account label of the account that this action is created for.|
|all_mastercard_action_refund|[[MasterCardActionRefund](#schemamastercardactionrefund)]|false|read-only|A reference to the Refunds if they exist.|
|amount_billing|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the transaction in the monetary account's currency.|
|amount_converted|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the transaction in local currency.|
|amount_fee|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The fee amount as charged by the merchant, if applicable.|
|amount_local|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the transaction in local currency.|
|amount_original_billing|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The original amount in the monetary account's currency.|
|amount_original_local|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The original amount in local currency.|
|applied_limit|string|false|read-only|The type of the limit applied to validate if this MasterCardAction was within the spending limits. The returned string matches the limit types as defined in the card endpoint.|
|authorisation_status|string|false|read-only|The status in the authorisation process.|
|authorisation_type|string|false|read-only|The type of transaction that was delivered using the card.|
|card_authorisation_id_response|string|false|read-only|The response code by which authorised transaction can be identified as authorised by bunq.|
|card_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the card this action links to.|
|city|string|false|read-only|The city where the message originates from as announced by the terminal.|
|clearing_expiry_time|string|false|read-only|The time when the processing of the clearing is expired, refunding the authorisation.|
|clearing_status|string|false|read-only|The clearing status of the authorisation. Can be 'PENDING', 'FIRST_PRESENTMENT_COMPLETE' or 'REFUND_LENIENCY'.|
|counterparty_alias|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The monetary account label of the counterparty.|
|decision|string|false|read-only|Why the transaction was denied, if it was denied, or just ALLOWED.|
|decision_description|string|false|read-only|Empty if allowed, otherwise a textual explanation of why it was denied.|
|decision_description_translated|string|false|read-only|Empty if allowed, otherwise a textual explanation of why it was denied in user's language.|
|decision_together_url|string|false|read-only|Empty if allowed or if no relevant Together topic exists, otherwise contains the URL for a Together topic with more information about the decision.|
|description|string|false|read-only|The description for this transaction to display.|
|eligible_whitelist_id|integer|false|read-only|The whitelist id for this action or null.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the MastercardAction.|
|label_card|[LabelCard](#schemalabelcard)|false|none|The label of the card.|
|maturity_date|string|false|read-only|The maturity date.|
|monetary_account_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the monetary account this action links to.|
|pan_entry_mode_user|string|false|read-only|The type of entry mode the user used. Can be 'ATM', 'ICC', 'MAGNETIC_STRIPE' or 'E_COMMERCE'.|
|payment_status|string|false|read-only|The payment status of the transaction. For example PAYMENT_SUCCESSFUL, for a successful payment.|
|pos_card_holder_presence|string|false|read-only|The Card Holder Presence type of the POS.|
|pos_card_presence|string|false|read-only|The Card Presence type of the POS.|
|request_reference_split_the_bill|[[RequestInquiryReference](#schemarequestinquiryreference)]|false|read-only|The reference to the object used for split the bill. Can be RequestInquiry or RequestInquiryBatch|
|reservation_expiry_time|string|false|read-only|If this is a reservation, the moment the reservation will expire.|
|secure_code_id|integer|false|read-only|The secure code id for this mastercard action or null.|
|settlement_status|string|false|read-only|The setlement status in the authorisation process.|
|token_status|string|false|read-only|If this is a tokenisation action, this shows the status of the token.|
|wallet_provider_id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the wallet provider as defined by MasterCard. 420 = bunq Android app with Tap&Pay; 103 = Apple Pay.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alias|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The monetary account label of the account that this action is created for.|
|all_mastercard_action_refund|[[MasterCardActionRefund](#schemamastercardactionrefund)]|false|read-only|A reference to the Refunds if they exist.|
|amount_billing|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the transaction in the monetary account's currency.|
|amount_converted|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the transaction in local currency.|
|amount_fee|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The fee amount as charged by the merchant, if applicable.|
|amount_local|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The amount of the transaction in local currency.|
|amount_original_billing|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The original amount in the monetary account's currency.|
|amount_original_local|[Amount](#schemaamount)|false|none|The original amount in local currency.|
|applied_limit|string|false|read-only|The type of the limit applied to validate if this MasterCardAction was within the spending limits. The returned string matches the limit types as defined in the card endpoint.|
|authorisation_status|string|false|read-only|The status in the authorisation process.|
|authorisation_type|string|false|read-only|The type of transaction that was delivered using the card.|
|card_authorisation_id_response|string|false|read-only|The response code by which authorised transaction can be identified as authorised by bunq.|
|card_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the card this action links to.|
|city|string|false|read-only|The city where the message originates from as announced by the terminal.|
|clearing_expiry_time|string|false|read-only|The time when the processing of the clearing is expired, refunding the authorisation.|
|clearing_status|string|false|read-only|The clearing status of the authorisation. Can be 'PENDING', 'FIRST_PRESENTMENT_COMPLETE' or 'REFUND_LENIENCY'.|
|counterparty_alias|[LabelMonetaryAccount](#schemalabelmonetaryaccount)|false|none|The monetary account label of the counterparty.|
|decision|string|false|read-only|Why the transaction was denied, if it was denied, or just ALLOWED.|
|decision_description|string|false|read-only|Empty if allowed, otherwise a textual explanation of why it was denied.|
|decision_description_translated|string|false|read-only|Empty if allowed, otherwise a textual explanation of why it was denied in user's language.|
|decision_together_url|string|false|read-only|Empty if allowed or if no relevant Together topic exists, otherwise contains the URL for a Together topic with more information about the decision.|
|description|string|false|read-only|The description for this transaction to display.|
|eligible_whitelist_id|integer|false|read-only|The whitelist id for this action or null.|
|id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the MastercardAction.|
|label_card|[LabelCard](#schemalabelcard)|false|none|The label of the card.|
|maturity_date|string|false|read-only|The maturity date.|
|monetary_account_id|integer|false|read-only|The id of the monetary account this action links to.|
|pan_entry_mode_user|string|false|read-only|The type of entry mode the user used. Can be 'ATM', 'ICC', 'MAGNETIC_STRIPE' or 'E_COMMERCE'.|
|payment_status|string|false|read-only|The payment status of the transaction. For example PAYMENT_SUCCESSFUL, for a successful payment.|
|pos_card_holder_presence|string|false|read-only|The Card Holder Presence type of the POS.|
|pos_card_presence|string|false|read-only|The Card Presence type of the POS.|
|request_reference_split_the_bill|[[RequestInquiryReference](#schemarequestinquiryreference)]|false|read-only|The reference to the object used for split the bill. Can be RequestInquiry or RequestInquiryBatch|
|reservation_expiry_time|string|false|read-only|If this is a reservation, the moment the reservation will expire.|
|secure_code_id|integer|false|read-only|The secure code id for this mastercard action or null.|
|settlement_status|string|false|read-only|The setlement status in the authorisation process.|
|token_status|string|false|read-only|If this is a tokenisation action, this shows the status of the token.|
|wallet_provider_id|string|false|read-only|The ID of the wallet provider as defined by MasterCard. 420 = bunq Android app with Tap&Pay; 103 = Apple Pay.|
